Section 20.4 sets standard reciprocal procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifier's expense, control of defence, settlement consent protections), and 20.5 provides the procure/modify-or-replace/terminate-and-refund remedies (cross-referenced by the termination right in 9.3). Customer's reverse indemnity in 20.3 stays narrow — unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorised and Customer's own violation of law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modifications, combinations and instructions. Indemnification obligations are Excluded Claims under 21.3, so they sit outside the general liability cap, which is better than the fallback's 3× super-cap. No redline needed.

The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of Fees "paid or payable" in the twelve months preceding the event and USD 1,000,000 (21.1); "Fees" (1.5) captures recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is meaningful rather than illusory. The consequential-damages exclusion is mutual and is improved for us by confirming data restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages (21.2). "Excluded Claims" sit outside both the cap and the exclusion and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP (21.3), and Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is expressly not "damages" limited by the Section. proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept non-solicitation or no-hire restrictions on us, so we have deleted § 12.4; it also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have given no no-hire commitment. If Vendor needs protection, we can accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services, for 12 months from the end of their involvement, with carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches and no restriction on hiring.
proposal.summary: Delete the one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-engage binding Customer (§ 12.4), consistent with § 12.3.

quote: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
rationale: § 12.4 imposes a one-way restriction on us only, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term (not just personnel involved in the services), extends to "engage" (an effective no-hire), and contains no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. It therefore fails the fallback on every material term (mutuality, scope, trigger, carve-outs, no no-hire) and the no-hire element edges into walk-away territory. It also conflicts with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no no-hire commitment. Redline deletes § 12.4 to reach the preferred position, with the narrow mutual fallback offered in the comment.
sectionRef: § 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not sol…

verification.notes: § 12.4 fails the fallback on every material term: it is one-way (binds only Customer), runs 18 months post-termination rather than 12 months from the end of involvement, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term rather than personnel directly involved in the services, extends to 'engage' (an effective no-hire, which the playbook treats as walk-away), and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Classification as a deviation is correct — this is not an acceptable fallback clause. Deletion of the entire paragraph validly reaches the preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer'); because the restriction is unilateral and includes a no-hire, narrowing edits alone could not cure mutuality or the walk-away no-hire element, so removal is a proportionate edit rather than over-reach. The comment is accurate on the facts of the clause (18 months, no-hire, no carve-out), states the playbook position concisely, and constructively offers the mutual 12-month/services-personnel/carve-out fallback, satisfying tone and actionability requirements. Failed deterministic checks (duration ≤ 12 months, carve-out present) are expected artifacts of a full deletion, not evidence of a defective edit; the redline is otherwise well-formed. Minor caveat: the cross-reference to § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgement that no no-hire commitment was given) is not verifiable from the supplied paragraphs — counsel should confirm before sending, but it does not undermine the finding.

quote: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form. Assistance includes knowledge transfer, export support, cooperation with a replacement supplier, orderly migration, and continued service at the then-current scope and service levels.
rationale: Section 11 meets the preferred position in all material respects: 11.1 gives up to six months' transition assistance on Customer's request at the expiring Order Form rates (better than "then-current rates" for us), 11.2 requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days in a complete, commonly used, documented machine-readable format and bars withholding data over a fee dispute, and 11.3 requires secure deletion only after Customer confirms successful return, with written officer certification and continuing protection of any legally retained copy. Sections 10.1-10.2 reinforce this with continuing rights in Customer Data, Deliverable delivery, and refunds of prepaid Fees. No walk-away features (no immediate deletion, no denial of data return). No redline needed.

quote: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
rationale: The warranty package meets the preferred position. Section 19.1 gives a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus material conformance to documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformance warranty (running from the later of delivery or acceptance) and a hosted-Services conformance warranty for the whole subscription term, which exceeds the 12-month software benchmark; 19.3 adds no-malicious-code and compliance-with-Applicable-Law warranties; and 19.4 supplies the full remedy ladder of prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, with termination and refund of Fees paid if Vendor cannot cure, expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims. The disclaimer in 19.5 is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties. No redline needed.

verification.notes: Claimed status is compliant and no redline or comment was proposed, which matches the expectation for a compliant finding — the paragraphs are returned unchanged. The cited text supports compliance with the preferred position: 19.1 gives the professional and workmanlike plus conformance warranty; 19.2 gives ninety days for Deliverables (from the later of delivery or acceptance) and conformance for hosted Services throughout the subscription term (exceeding the 12-month software benchmark); 19.3 covers no malicious code and compliance with Applicable Law; 19.4 supplies the re-perform/repair/replace and refund remedy ladder. The disclaimer in 19.5 is confined to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or stated remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranties — no walk-away 'AS IS' risk. The failed deterministic check is a phrasing artifact: the period is written out as 'ninety days' rather than numerically, so the ≥90-day threshold is in fact satisfied and the check should not override the substantive reading. Rationale is accurate and cites the correct paragraphs; no over- or under-statement warranting a severity adjustment.
